newsitem.title: USA: Manufactured Home sues Chateau, ROC.
newsitem.headline: Manufactured Home sues Chateau, ROC.

text.p: Chicago developer Samuel Zell's Manufactured Home Communities Inc. said Wednesday it was suing rival mobile home park operators Chateau Properties Inc. and ROC Communities Inc. to block their proposed merger.
Chateau last week announced a revised merger deal with its original partner ROC, and rejected Manufactured Home's $400 million, $26-a-share, takeover bid as inadequate.
It also said the long-term benefits of a combination with ROC were superior to a merger with Sun Communities Inc., another suitor which had offered $390 million.
"We are forced to take this action in response to the drastic steps taken last week by Chateau and ROC," said Zell, who is chairman of Manufactured Home.
"Their restructured merger disenfranchises Chateau's shareholders and ultimately reallocates tax liability from Chateau insiders to the shareholders."
The suit, filed in a Maryland district court, also names Chateau board members John Boll, C.G. Kellogg, Jay Rudolph, Gebran Anton Jr., James Lane, Kenneth Myers and Edward Allen as defendants.
Manufactured Home's stock rose 12.5 cents to $19.125 on the New York Stock Exchange. Chateau climbed 37.5 cents to $25.375, while Sun edged up 37.5 cents to $28.25, also on the NYSE.
